historical-0c9d698dd3306b18d84fa64b.title: Apple Sauce with Butter
historical-0c9d698dd3306b18d84fa64b.description: Tart apples are simmered and mashed, then finished with butter and a little sugar for a smooth accompaniment.

ingredients.name: tart apples, weighed after peeling and coring
ingredients.substitution: Use the same prepared weight of another cooking apple; sweetness and the time needed to soften will vary.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened apple juice for a sweeter sauce with a different flavor.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a dairy-free butter alternative, or omit for a less rich sauce.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Reduce to taste for a less sweet sauce; this is a refrigerated food, not a shelf-stable preserve.

steps: Cut {{apples}} into roughly 2 cm pieces. Put them in a heavy saucepan with {{water}}.

Bring just to a boil, cover and lower the heat. Simmer for 15–25 minutes, stirring frequently, until the apples collapse easily under a spoon. Add a small splash of water only if the pan begins to dry.
Mash the apples with a potato masher, or press through a sieve for a smoother sauce.
Stir {{butter}} and {{sugar}} into the hot mashed apples until melted and dissolved.
Serve warm, or transfer to shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours at 4°C (40°F) or colder. Freeze portions for longer storage. This is not a canning recipe.
historical-0c9d698dd3306b18d84fa64b.notes: Two six-apple sources have the same butter-and-sugar finish. Prepared apple weight replaces variable fruit size. Water is increased from the Abbott source spoonful to a practical 120 ml to limit scorching; the Beeton source gives no fixed water quantity. Both sources are retained. Missing amounts, portion yields and timings are disclosed modern estimates, not exact recovered historical measurements. Not kitchen-tested. Scaling changes quantities, not cooking time or temperature.
historical-0c9d698dd3306b18d84fa64b.source: The English and Australian Cookery Book (1864), Edward Abbott. https://archive.org/details/b21505524 SavorShelf measured adaptation. Apple preparation and simmering reference: https://extension.rutgers.edu/recipes/applesauce Equivalent source retained: The Book of Household Management (1861), Isabella Beeton. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10136

historical-f8ae338a990b1599597520f3.title: Buttered Toast
historical-f8ae338a990b1599597520f3.description: Thick bread is toasted crisp and buttered on both faces while hot, leaving a crunchy surface and a tender middle.

ingredients.name: bread, each about 19 mm (¾ inch) thick
ingredients.substitution: Use the same number of similarly sized wheat, white or sourdough slices. Gluten-free bread may toast faster.

ingredients.name: softened salted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a spreadable dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and browning differ.

steps: Arrange {{bread}} on a rack over a baking tray. Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toast for about 6–10 minutes, turning halfway, until both faces are crisp and golden. Watch the final minutes closely.
Spread {{butter|0.5}} over one face of the warm slices. Turn them over and spread the remaining {{butter|0.5}} over the other face.
Serve two slices per person immediately. For a larger batch, toast in uncrowded batches; do not multiply the oven temperature or per-batch time.
historical-f8ae338a990b1599597520f3.notes: The source specified bread thickness and buttering both sides but no quantities. This adaptation sets four slices, 28 g butter and an oven method. Bread size changes the portion size. Yield and timing are planning estimates. This adaptation has not been kitchen-tested.
historical-f8ae338a990b1599597520f3.source: The English and Australian Cookery Book (1864), Edward Abbott. https://archive.org/details/b21505524 Modern adaptation by SavorShelf.

historical-08848a853895b5dcff651cf2.title: Melted Butter Sauce with Milk
historical-08848a853895b5dcff651cf2.description: A rich butter sauce uses a little milk and water with flour to give a smooth, lightly thickened finish.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

ingredients.name: all-purpose wheat flour
ingredients.substitution: Use an equal weight of a gluten-free all-purpose blend intended for sauces; texture can differ. Do not replace with an equal weight of cornstarch.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened soy milk for a dairy-free variation; flavor and thickening may differ.

ingredients.name: cold drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Unsalted vegetable stock may replace the same volume in a savory sauce, changing its flavor.

steps: Whisk {{flour}} with {{milk|0.25}} in a small saucepan until smooth.
Gradually whisk in the remaining {{milk|0.75}} and {{water}}, then add {{butter}} in small pieces.
Return to medium-low heat, whisking until the sauce gently bubbles. Lower the heat and cook 5 minutes, stirring along the bottom, until smooth and thickened. Avoid a hard boil.
Serve warm. If too thick after standing, whisk in a small splash of the recipe’s liquid to restore the intended pouring consistency.
historical-08848a853895b5dcff651cf2.notes: The source butter quantity is about 56 g; its dessertspoon and tablespoons are assigned modern amounts. Serve freshly made; scaling changes quantities, not temperature or cooking time.

historical-b145dc6352fdda9a9d8433fb.title: Melted Butter Sauce — Light Water Base
historical-b145dc6352fdda9a9d8433fb.description: A water-based flour sauce is finished with butter, giving a light savory coating without milk.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

ingredients.name: all-purpose wheat flour
ingredients.substitution: Use an equal weight of a gluten-free all-purpose blend intended for sauces; texture can differ. Do not replace with an equal weight of cornstarch.

ingredients.name: cold drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Unsalted vegetable stock may replace the same volume in a savory sauce, changing its flavor.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit, especially when using salted butter or stock; exchange other salt by weight.

steps: Melt {{butter|0.5}} in a small heavy saucepan over low heat. Stir in {{flour}} and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes without browning.
Take off the heat and whisk in {{water}} a little at a time until smooth.
Return to medium-low heat, whisking until the sauce gently bubbles. Lower the heat and cook 5 minutes, stirring along the bottom, until smooth and thickened. Avoid a hard boil.
Mix in {{salt}}.
Remove from the heat and whisk in the remaining {{butter|0.5}}.
Serve warm. If too thick after standing, whisk in a small splash of the recipe’s liquid to restore the intended pouring consistency.
historical-b145dc6352fdda9a9d8433fb.notes: The truncated method is completed. Half the butter cooks the flour; the remaining half finishes the sauce. Water is a modern 500 ml batch, not an asserted pint conversion. Missing or ambiguous source amounts, modern ingredient choices, sauce portions and timings are explicit adaptation estimates, not exact recovered historical measurements. Not kitchen-tested. Serve freshly made; scaling changes quantities, not temperature or cooking time.

historical-7b625429ab109be7ae379461.title: Potatoes Finished in White Sauce
historical-7b625429ab109be7ae379461.description: Thin potato slices finish cooking in a light butter-and-milk sauce, making a soft, creamy side dish.

ingredients.name: peeled waxy potatoes, cut into 5 mm slices
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of another firm boiling potato; floury potatoes may break apart.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: No replacement is needed; increase cooking water only as needed to cover the food.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit; exchange other salt by weight rather than spoon size.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit; exchange other salt by weight rather than spoon size.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened soy milk; flavor and thickening may differ.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

ingredients.name: all-purpose wheat flour
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a gluten-free all-purpose blend intended for sauces; texture may differ. Cornstarch is not a weight-for-weight replacement.

ingredients.name: ground white pepper
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of black pepper for visible specks, or omit.

steps: Bring {{water}} and {{boilsalt}} to a boil. Add {{potatoes}} and simmer for 5 minutes, then drain. The slices will finish cooking in the sauce.
Melt {{butter}} in a separate saucepan over low heat. Stir in {{flour}} and cook for 2 minutes without browning.
Take off the heat and gradually whisk in {{milk}} until smooth. Return to medium-low heat and stir until gently bubbling. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring along the bottom.

Add {{salt}} and {{pepper}} to the sauce. Gently fold in the partly cooked potatoes. Simmer over low heat for 10–15 minutes, stirring carefully, until a knife passes easily through a slice. Add a splash of water only if the sauce catches or becomes too thick. Serve hot.
historical-7b625429ab109be7ae379461.notes: The missing white-sauce cross-reference is expanded using a thin milk sauce. Potato and pint quantities are practical modern amounts. Missing amounts, portion yields and timings are modern adaptation estimates, not recovered historical measurements. Not kitchen-tested. Scaling changes ingredient quantities, not cooking time or temperature.

historical-d8027a619a1091584dab1f1f.title: Cut Asparagus in White Sauce
historical-d8027a619a1091584dab1f1f.description: Tender asparagus pieces are folded through a smooth milk sauce for a lightly coated vegetable side.

ingredients.name: fresh asparagus, tough lower ends trimmed
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of green beans for a different dish; cook until tender, usually 5–7 minutes.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: No replacement is needed; increase cooking water only as needed to cover the food.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit; exchange other salt by weight rather than spoon size.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened soy milk; flavor and thickening may differ.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

ingredients.name: all-purpose wheat flour
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a gluten-free all-purpose blend intended for sauces; texture may differ. Cornstarch is not a weight-for-weight replacement.

steps: Cut {{asparagus}} into 2.5 cm pieces. Bring {{water}} and {{salt|0.75}} to a boil. Cook the stem pieces for 2 minutes, add the tips and cook another 1–3 minutes until just tender. Drain well.
Melt {{butter}} in a separate saucepan over low heat. Stir in {{flour}} and cook for 2 minutes without browning.
Take off the heat and gradually whisk in {{milk}} until smooth. Return to medium-low heat and stir until gently bubbling. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring along the bottom.
Stir {{salt|0.25}} into the sauce. Fold in the drained asparagus and warm for 1 minute without crushing it. Serve immediately.
historical-d8027a619a1091584dab1f1f.notes: The source lacks amounts and a sauce formula; both are supplied. Cut-and-coated presentation is retained, distinct from whole spears with sauce served separately. historical-cda7984d1940ec11751a07e6.title: Slow-Baked Brown-Sugar Apple Sauce
historical-cda7984d1940ec11751a07e6.description: Covered apples bake slowly with brown sugar until soft and concentrated.

ingredients.name: medium firm apples, about 180 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use another firm apple of similar size; cooking time and sweetness differ.

ingredients.name: light brown sugar
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of the other sugar for a different flavor, or reduce to taste.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened apple juice for a sweeter fruit dish.

steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (320°F). Peel and core {{apples}}, then cut into 2 cm pieces.
Put the fruit in a covered ovenproof casserole with {{sugar}} and {{water}}. Stir, cover and bake for 90 minutes.
Stir carefully and continue for 30–60 minutes, uncovering for the last 20 minutes if too wet, until very soft and reduced. Add a splash of water if the edges catch.
Mash to the desired texture and serve warm, or cool promptly in shallow containers and refrigerate.
historical-cda7984d1940ec11751a07e6.notes: A practical six-apple batch and controlled oven temperature are supplied. Color varies by apple variety; softness and concentration determine doneness, not a guaranteed red color. Water is supplied to prevent scorching. Missing quantities, yields and timings are disclosed modern estimates, not recovered historical measures. Not kitchen-tested. Scaling changes quantities, not time or temperature. Refrigerate in shallow containers within 2 hours at 4°C (40°F) or colder; freeze for longer storage. Not a canning recipe.
historical-cda7984d1940ec11751a07e6.source: Canadian Farm Cook Book (1911), author not recorded. https://archive.org/details/canadianfarmcook00unse SavorShelf measured adaptation.

historical-e9e191da245c8c1e2b9cacee.title: Spiced Crabapple Sauce for Meat
historical-e9e191da245c8c1e2b9cacee.description: Tart crabapples are cooked with vinegar, brown sugar and warming spices into a sweet-sour condiment.

ingredients.name: crabapples, washed, stemmed and cored
ingredients.substitution: Use 454 g prepared tart cooking apples for a less sharp sauce.

ingredients.name: cider vinegar labeled 5% acidity
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of white wine vinegar for a different flavor.

ingredients.name: brown sugar
ingredients.substitution: Use 454 g granulated sugar for a lighter flavor.

ingredients.name: ground cinnamon
ingredients.substitution: Use half as much ground allspice for a different flavor, or omit.

ingredients.name: ground cloves
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit for a milder condiment.

ingredients.name: ground black pepper
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit.

ingredients.name: fine table salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit; do not substitute coarse salt by equal volume.

steps: Cut {{apples}} into small pieces and put in a nonreactive saucepan with {{vinegar}}. Simmer for 20–30 minutes until completely soft.
Press through a sieve into a clean pan, discarding coarse skins. Add {{sugar}}, {{cinnamon}}, {{cloves}}, {{pepper}} and {{salt}}.
Simmer gently for 5–10 minutes, stirring frequently, until the sugar dissolves and the sauce lightly coats a spoon. Add a little vinegar if it becomes too thick.
Transfer to shallow containers, cool briefly and refrigerate. Serve in small condiment portions.
historical-e9e191da245c8c1e2b9cacee.notes: A one-third batch retains the equal fruit-and-sugar weights. A modern 480 ml vinegar and 2/3 teaspoon spices replace uncertain quart/dessertspoon measures. Hot bottling is replaced by refrigeration; no shelf-stability is claimed. Yield is estimated condiment portions, not main servings. Missing quantities, yields and timings are disclosed modern estimates, not recovered historical measures. Not kitchen-tested. Scaling changes quantities, not time or temperature. Refrigerate in shallow containers within 2 hours at 4°C (40°F) or colder; freeze for longer storage. Not a canning recipe.
historical-e9e191da245c8c1e2b9cacee.source: Canadian Farm Cook Book (1911), author not recorded. https://archive.org/details/canadianfarmcook00unse SavorShelf measured adaptation.

historical-7b50009f683c2e6110a9c62e.title: Mashed Potatoes
historical-7b50009f683c2e6110a9c62e.description: Steamed potatoes are mashed with warm milk and a little butter for a soft, light side dish, with optional oven browning.

ingredients.name: peeled floury potatoes, cut into 3 cm chunks
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of russet potatoes; Yukon Gold gives a denser, creamier mash.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a dairy-free butter alternative.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of lactose-free whole milk. Unsweetened plant milk changes the flavor.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Omit for an unsalted version; do not exchange different salts by volume.

steps: Cover {{potatoes}} with cold water and leave for 30 minutes, as in the source; then drain.

Put the potato pieces in a steamer over simmering water, keeping them above the water. Cover and steam for 20–25 minutes until a fork meets no resistance. Keep water in the lower pan as needed for steaming.
Warm {{milk}} in a small saucepan until steaming, without boiling. Transfer the tender potatoes to a warm bowl and mash by hand.
Mix {{butter}} and {{salt}} into the hot mash. Stir in half the warm milk, {{milk|0.5}}, followed by the remaining {{milk|0.5}}, until evenly combined. Avoid a blender or food processor.
Serve as six side portions. For the optional browned finish, place in a shallow oven-safe dish and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 10–15 minutes.
historical-7b50009f683c2e6110a9c62e.notes: The missing potato weight and salt amount are supplied as a modern formulation. Milk and butter are interpreted as 240 ml and 14 g. The original soak and steaming method are retained. Allow about 70 minutes without browning, or 85 with it. Yield and timing are planning estimates. This adaptation has not been kitchen-tested.
historical-7b50009f683c2e6110a9c62e.source: Canadian Farm Cook Book (1911), author not recorded. https://archive.org/details/canadianfarmcook00unse Modern adaptation by SavorShelf. Mashing technique cross-check: https://www.idahopotato.com/recipes/traditional-mashed-idaho-potatoes ; quantities and steaming method above are this source adaptation, not that recipe.

historical-2e7e500ab29342109640c6c3.title: Onions in White Sauce
historical-2e7e500ab29342109640c6c3.description: Quartered onions are boiled until tender and coated in a milk sauce thickened with butter kneaded with flour.

ingredients.name: medium onions, about 600 g peeled in total
ingredients.substitution: Use 600 g peeled small onions or shallots; adjust cooking until tender.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: No replacement is needed; increase cooking water only as needed to cover the food.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened soy milk; flavor and thickening may differ.

ingredients.name: all-purpose wheat flour
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a gluten-free all-purpose blend intended for sauces; texture may differ. Cornstarch is not a weight-for-weight replacement.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

steps: Peel and quarter {{onions}}. Bring {{water}} to a boil, add the onions and simmer for about 20 minutes until a knife pierces them easily. Drain well.
Mash softened {{butter}} with {{flour}} to make an even paste with no dry flour.
Heat {{milk}} in a saucepan until steaming. Whisk in the butter-flour paste a small piece at a time, then simmer gently for 5 minutes, stirring, until smooth and lightly thickened.
Fold the drained onions into the sauce and warm gently for 2 minutes. Serve hot.
historical-2e7e500ab29342109640c6c3.notes: The source five onions and kneaded-butter method are retained. Cups and spoonfuls are assigned modern measured amounts; onion size is clarified. Missing amounts, portion yields and timings are modern adaptation estimates, not recovered historical measurements. Not kitchen-tested. Scaling changes ingredient quantities, not cooking time or temperature.
historical-2e7e500ab29342109640c6c3.source: Canadian Farm Cook Book (1911), author not recorded. https://archive.org/details/canadianfarmcook00unse SavorShelf measured adaptation.

historical-dd8c7e4f64772fa37bb54bed.title: Scrambled Eggs
historical-dd8c7e4f64772fa37bb54bed.description: Eggs scrambled in butter with a small splash of milk form tender curds. The source’s generous pepper amount gives a pronounced peppery finish.

ingredients.name: large eggs
ingredients.substitution: Use pasteurized shell eggs in the same number if preferred. An egg-free replacement needs a separate formulation.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.substitution: Use 30 ml water for a less creamy result, or the same volume of lactose-free milk.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit to taste; salt does not provide the structure here.

ingredients.name: ground black pepper
ingredients.substitution: Use less if desired; the original recipe is strongly peppered. White pepper has a different flavor.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a dairy-free butter alternative; flavor will differ.

steps: Whisk {{eggs}}, {{milk}}, {{salt}} and {{pepper}} in a bowl until evenly combined.
Melt {{butter}} in a large nonstick frying pan over medium-low heat; do not let it brown.
Pour in the egg mixture. Move a spatula slowly across the base and fold the setting curds over, cooking about 3–5 minutes until the eggs are set and no liquid egg remains.
Remove from the heat and divide into three portions. Serve immediately; the pan’s retained heat continues to firm the eggs.
historical-dd8c7e4f64772fa37bb54bed.notes: This adaptation keeps the six-egg formula, interprets the old milk and butter measures in metric, supplies weighed seasoning and a three-portion yield, and clarifies heat and doneness. Pan size and stove heat affect timing. Yield and timing are planning estimates. This adaptation has not been kitchen-tested.
historical-dd8c7e4f64772fa37bb54bed.source: Canadian Farm Cook Book (1911), author not recorded. https://archive.org/details/canadianfarmcook00unse Modern adaptation by SavorShelf. Technique cross-check: https://www.incredibleegg.org/recipe/basic-scrambled-eggs/ ; this retains the historical formula rather than the reference recipe’s proportions.

historical-4ed07776bd7c100f03b9a6c2.title: Brambory vařené (Boiled Potatoes)
historical-4ed07776bd7c100f03b9a6c2.description: Peeled potatoes receive the source’s cold soak, then simmer until tender and finish with salt and a covered rest.

ingredients.name: peeled potatoes, cut into equal 3 cm pieces
ingredients.substitution: Use a similarly sized potato with the same texture: waxy for intact pieces; floury for ricing. Large whole potatoes need longer cooking.

ingredients.name: cooking water
ingredients.substitution: Use drinking water; stock changes the flavor and salt level. Rinsing water is separate and is discarded.

steps: Prepare {{potatoes}}. Remove sprouts and damaged or green areas; discard extensively green potatoes. Cover with separate cold rinsing water for 1 hour, then drain.
Bring {{water}} to a boil in a saucepan that holds the potatoes comfortably. Carefully add the potatoes; water should just cover them. If necessary, add enough hot water to cover.
Reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook about 20–25 minutes, until a thin knife enters the center without resistance. Do not use time alone as the test.
Drain carefully and return to the warm pan off the heat. Sprinkle with {{salt}} and gently shake. Cover and leave 5 minutes, as in the source.

ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of lime juice for a different citrus flavor.

steps: Rinse {{apples}}, peel and remove every core and seed. Cut into halves.
In a snug pan, heat {{water}} with {{sugar}}, {{lemon}}, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add the apples in one layer, working in batches if needed.

Cover and simmer gently, turning carefully halfway through, until a knife enters easily but the fruit holds its shape: about 10–20 minutes. Baste frequently; add a little water if the liquid becomes too thick before the fruit softens.
Lift the apples onto a serving dish. Simmer the liquid uncovered for 3–8 minutes until lightly syrupy, then spoon it over the fruit.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve warm, or refrigerate promptly for serving cold.

historical-ab6b4890fba0b53e6d07646e.description: Whole globe artichokes are cooked until tender and served with a separate smooth milk sauce for dipping the leaves and heart.

ingredients.name: medium globe artichokes
ingredients.substitution: Use four large drained canned artichoke hearts for a smaller shortcut dish; warm them separately and omit whole-artichoke preparation and boiling.

ingredients.substitution: No replacement is needed; increase cooking water only as needed to cover the food.

steps: Rinse {{artichokes}}. Trim the stems to about 1 cm, remove the small tough lower leaves and cut about 2 cm off the tops. Snip off sharp leaf tips with kitchen scissors.

Bring {{water}} to a boil in a pot that holds the artichokes comfortably, adding more water if needed to cover. Add the artichokes and simmer, loosely covered, for 30–45 minutes, until a leaf pulls away easily and a knife enters the base without resistance.
Lift out and drain upside down. When cool enough to handle, gently open the centers and scoop out the fuzzy choke with a spoon; do not eat the fuzzy material. Keep the tender bases and leaves intact.
Melt {{butter}} in a separate saucepan over low heat. Stir in {{flour}} and cook for 2 minutes without browning.
Take off the heat and gradually whisk in {{milk}} until smooth. Return to medium-low heat and stir until gently bubbling. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring along the bottom.

Stir {{salt}} into the sauce. Serve the warm artichokes with the sauce alongside. Pull off each leaf and scrape the tender flesh at its base with your teeth; discard the tough leaf. Eat the tender heart after the leaves.
historical-ab6b4890fba0b53e6d07646e.notes: Two sources share whole cooked artichokes and white sauce. The Mexican source’s brief cooling and reheating presentation is retained as a named variation. steps: Mix {{soakwater}} with {{vinegar|0.5}} in a bowl. Scrub and peel {{salsify}}, trim the ends and cut into 7 cm lengths, placing each piece immediately in the acidulated water to limit browning.
Put {{water}}, {{vinegar|0.5}}, {{fat}} and {{boilsalt}} in a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer. Drain the salsify from its soaking water and add it to the pan.
Simmer until a knife enters easily but the roots still hold their shape, checking after 8 minutes; thick pieces may need 15–25 minutes. Drain and discard the cooking liquid.
Melt {{butter}} in a separate saucepan over low heat. Stir in {{flour}} and cook for 2 minutes without browning.
Take off the heat and gradually whisk in {{milk}} until smooth. Return to medium-low heat and stir until gently bubbling. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring along the bottom.
Stir {{salt}} into the sauce. Fold in the hot drained salsify and serve.

Rendered beef fat replaces raw kidney fat and a tenderness check replaces a rigid half-hour boil. The cooking fat and liquid are largely discarded. Sauce quantities are supplied. ingredients.substitution: Use an equal weight of a gluten-free all-purpose blend intended for sauces; texture can differ. Do not replace with an equal weight of cornstarch.

steps: Whisk {{flour}} into {{water}} in a saucepan until smooth. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring continuously, and cook 10 minutes over low heat.
Remove from the heat and whisk in {{fat}}, {{salt}} and {{pepper}} until incorporated.
Whisk {{yolk}} with {{liaison}} in a bowl. Gradually whisk a few spoonfuls of warm sauce into the yolk mixture, then return it to the saucepan.
Stir over low heat until the sauce reaches 71°C (160°F), without boiling. Serve immediately.

steps: Put {{potatoes}} in a pan with {{water}} and {{salt|0.75}}, adding water only if needed to cover. Bring to a gentle boil and cook for 20–30 minutes until a knife passes through easily. Drain, cool just enough to handle, peel and cut into 1 cm slices.

Melt {{butter}} in a wide pan. Cook {{onion}} over medium-low heat for 5 minutes until soft. Add {{tomato}} and cook for 3 minutes, then add the potato slices and cook gently for another 3 minutes, turning carefully.
Whisk {{flour}} with {{saucewater}} until smooth. Pour into the pan, add {{salt|0.25}} and simmer gently for 5 minutes, stirring carefully, until lightly thickened and the potatoes are hot.
Scatter over {{parsley}} and serve immediately.

historical-9aef2d2ba3e4e7ee9208ef50.title: Peras con Vino Tinto (Red-Wine Pears)
historical-9aef2d2ba3e4e7ee9208ef50.description: Whole pears cook with cinnamon and cloves, with red wine added partway through for a richly flavored syrup.

ingredients.name: medium firm pears, about 170 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use firm pears of similar size; dessert pears soften sooner than hard winter cooking varieties. Check tenderness rather than relying only on time.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened pear juice in a fruit dish for a sweeter flavor.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Reduce for a less sweet result; this is not a shelf-stable preserve.

ingredients.name: small cinnamon stick
ingredients.substitution: Use 0.25 tsp ground cinnamon per stick; leave ground spice in the sauce.

ingredients.name: whole cloves
ingredients.substitution: Omit for a milder dish, or use 0.1 g ground cloves per whole clove and leave in the sauce.

ingredients.name: dry red wine
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened red grape juice for an alcohol-free but sweeter variation.

steps: Rinse {{pears}}. Leave the skins on. Scoop out the cores and seeds from the base with a melon baller, keeping the pears whole.
Put {{water}} and {{sugar}} in a snug saucepan with {{cinnamon}}, {{cloves}}. Heat gently, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add the pears in one layer, working in batches if needed.

After the first 15 minutes of gentle cooking, add {{wine}}. Cover and simmer very gently, turning and basting carefully, until a small knife enters the flesh easily: 25–45 minutes for whole pears. Add a little water if the pan dries before the fruit softens.
Lift out the pears. Remove any whole spices or zest strips. Simmer the liquid uncovered for 5–10 minutes until lightly syrupy, then spoon it over the fruit.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve warm, or cool promptly and refrigerate.
historical-9aef2d2ba3e4e7ee9208ef50.notes: Equivalent Mexican and French formulas are consolidated. The source glasses become 240 ml each. Wine remains alcoholic after cooking. historical-6dbf1c7aa4b6004cc3bfbd38.description: Pears absorb syrup over three days, then are filled with coconut paste and browned under a thick almond-custard coating.

ingredients.name: small firm pears, weighed after peeling and coring, about four
ingredients.substitution: Use firm small pears that hold their shape; soft ripe pears are unsuitable for repeated heating.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Reduce for a less sweet result; this is not a shelf-stable preserve.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened pear juice in a fruit dish for a sweeter flavor.

ingredients.name: unsweetened desiccated coconut
ingredients.substitution: Use 50 g finely ground almonds for a different filling, noting almonds are also in the coating.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Reduce for a less sweet result; this is not a shelf-stable preserve.

ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened pear juice in a fruit dish for a sweeter flavor.

ingredients.substitution: Use 18 g pasteurized liquid yolk per large yolk; an egg-free version needs a different thickening method.

ingredients.substitution: Reduce for a less sweet result; this is not a shelf-stable preserve.

steps: Day 1: Prepare {{pears}}, leaving the fruit whole with a cavity for filling. Dissolve {{sugar}} in {{water}} in a snug saucepan. Add the pears and simmer very gently for 20–35 minutes, turning carefully, until just tender but intact.

Transfer pears and syrup to shallow heatproof containers. Cool briefly and refrigerate within 2 hours at 4°C (40°F) or colder. Leave refrigerated overnight; never hold the fruit overnight at room temperature.
Day 2: Return fruit and syrup to the pan, heat gently to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes. Cool and refrigerate again as on day 1.
Day 3: Gently simmer fruit and syrup for another 10 minutes. Lift the pears onto a rack over a tray to drain. Measure {{reserved}} for the coating; cool and refrigerate the unused syrup separately.
Cook {{coconut}}, {{fillsugar}} and {{fillwater}} in a small pan for 3–5 minutes, stirring until a thick moist paste forms. Let cool enough to handle and spoon into the pear cavities.
Whisk {{starch}} and {{custardsugar}} into {{milk}} in a small saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer while whisking and cook for 1 minute. Remove from the heat.
Whisk {{yolks}} in a bowl. Slowly whisk in a little hot milk mixture, then return to the pan. Stir over low heat until the custard reaches 82°C (180°F), without boiling.
Stir {{almonds}} and the reserved syrup into the warm custard. Cook gently, stirring for 2–3 minutes, until thick enough to coat the pears; do not boil.
Heat the oven grill/broiler. Place the filled pears in a metal baking dish, coat with the almond custard and brown briefly 15–20 cm below the heat, about 2–4 minutes, watching constantly. Serve warm.
historical-6dbf1c7aa4b6004cc3bfbd38.notes: The shorter duplicate transcription is completed from the fuller same-book recipe. Equal prepared fruit/sugar weights and three-day absorption are retained; shorter controlled reheats replace repeated multi-hour boils. Coconut paste, custard and coating quantities are supplied. Bricks, stones and the historical overhead brazier are equipment, not ingredients; a modern broiler replaces them. Total time includes two overnight refrigerator holds. Missing amounts, oven settings, yields and timings are explicit modern adaptation estimates, not exact historical conversions. Not kitchen-tested. historical-f6eefd602cae2e8e252d4b24.title: Compota de Peras Tostadas (Roasted and Poached Pears)
historical-f6eefd602cae2e8e252d4b24.description: Pears are roasted until their skins loosen, then peeled and finished in cinnamon syrup.

ingredients.name: medium firm pears, about 170 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use firm pears of similar size; dessert pears soften sooner than hard winter cooking varieties. Check tenderness rather than relying only on time.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened pear juice in a fruit dish for a sweeter flavor.

ingredients.substitution: Reduce for a less sweet result; this is not a shelf-stable preserve.

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (428°F). Rinse {{pears}} and place on a rimmed metal tray. Roast for 20–30 minutes, turning once, until the skins blister and loosen; do not deliberately char the flesh.
Cool just enough to handle. Peel away the loosened skins, halve the pears and remove all cores and seeds.
Heat {{water}}, {{sugar}} and {{cinnamon}} in a saucepan until dissolved. Add the pear halves and simmer for 10–25 minutes until tender.
Lift out the pears, discard the cinnamon stick and simmer the liquid for 5–10 minutes until syrupy. Spoon over the fruit and serve.
historical-f6eefd602cae2e8e252d4b24.notes: Equivalent toasted-pear methods are consolidated. A four-pear batch and measured syrup replace unclear source quantities. Controlled roasting replaces burning the skins over an open fire; the roast-then-poach sequence remains. Missing amounts, oven settings, yields and timings are explicit modern adaptation estimates, not exact historical conversions. Not kitchen-tested. historical-9ae9cf59965859c5b35394d1.title: Perones Encantullados (Candied Apples with Spices)
historical-9ae9cf59965859c5b35394d1.description: Firm apples absorb sugar syrup over three days and finish with clove and cinnamon, without the filled pear recipe’s stuffing.

ingredients.name: firm perón apples, peeled and cored, about four
ingredients.substitution: Use another firm tart cooking apple; avoid varieties that collapse quickly.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar

ingredients.substitution: Omit for a milder dish, or use 0.1 g ground cloves per whole clove and leave in the sauce.

ingredients.name: small cinnamon sticks, broken into short pieces
ingredients.substitution: Use 0.75 tsp ground cinnamon, leaving it in the syrup.

steps: Dissolve {{sugar}} in {{water}} in a snug saucepan. Add {{apples}} and simmer very gently for 15–25 minutes until just tender but intact, turning carefully.
Transfer fruit and syrup to shallow containers, cool briefly and refrigerate within 2 hours at 4°C (40°F) or colder. Leave overnight.
On the next day, heat fruit and syrup gently to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes. Cool and refrigerate overnight again.

On day 3, add {{cloves}} and {{cinnamon}} to the syrup and simmer gently for 10 minutes. Lift out the apples, remove all whole spices and reduce the syrup for 5–10 minutes if needed. Spoon over the fruit and serve.

historical-b2d13dcc73a73d8b97f5c091.title: Huevos Escalfados en Crema (Eggs in Cream)
historical-b2d13dcc73a73d8b97f5c091.description: Whole eggs bake gently with cream and butter in individual dishes for a rich, spoonable breakfast.

ingredients.name: large hen eggs
ingredients.substitution: Use large pasteurized shell eggs for a soft-yolk option. Liquid egg substitute cannot retain this whole-egg shape.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of dairy-free butter alternative; check its salt content.

ingredients.name: fine salt

ingredients.name: heavy cream

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease two ovenproof 150–200 ml ramekins with {{butter|0.5}} and set on a baking tray.
Warm {{cream}} with the remaining {{butter|0.5}} until the butter melts; mix in {{salt}}.
Crack {{eggs}}, one into each ramekin. Divide the warm cream mixture around them.
Bake 12–18 minutes, checking from 12 minutes, and continue until whites and yolks are firm. Serve on plates beneath the hot ramekins.

ingredients.name: jointed farm-raised rabbit, bone-in
ingredients.substitution: Use 1200 g bone-in chicken thighs for a different dish; cook chicken to 74°C (165°F).

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce, particularly if using salted stock.

steps: Mix {{rabbit}} with {{salt}}, {{garlic}}, {{pepper}} and {{tomatoes}} in a covered nonreactive container. Refrigerate at 4°C (40°F) or colder for 24 hours.

historical-96706fae3cc20a4530240f3c.title: Peras à Borguinhona (Burgundy-Style Pears)
historical-96706fae3cc20a4530240f3c.description: Unpeeled pears are gently cooked with cinnamon and cloves, then finished with a smaller red-wine addition.

ingredients.name: medium firm pears, about 170 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use firm pears of similar size; dessert pears soften sooner than hard winter cooking varieties. Check tenderness rather than relying only on time.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened pear juice in a fruit dish for a sweeter flavor.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Reduce for a less sweet result; this is not a shelf-stable preserve.

ingredients.name: small cinnamon stick
ingredients.substitution: Use 0.25 tsp ground cinnamon per stick; leave ground spice in the sauce.

ingredients.name: whole cloves
ingredients.substitution: Omit for a milder dish, or use 0.1 g ground cloves per whole clove and leave in the sauce.

ingredients.name: dry red wine
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened red grape juice for an alcohol-free but sweeter variation.

steps: Rinse {{pears}}. Leave the skins on. Scoop out the cores and seeds from the base with a melon baller, keeping the pears whole.
Put {{water}} and {{sugar}} in a snug saucepan with {{cinnamon}}, {{cloves}}. Heat gently, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add the pears in one layer, working in batches if needed.

After the first 15 minutes of gentle cooking, add {{wine}}. Cover and simmer very gently, turning and basting carefully, until a small knife enters the flesh easily: 25–45 minutes for whole pears. Add a little water if the pan dries before the fruit softens.
Lift out the pears. Remove any whole spices or zest strips. Simmer the liquid uncovered for 5–10 minutes until lightly syrupy, then spoon it over the fruit.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve warm, or cool promptly and refrigerate.
historical-96706fae3cc20a4530240f3c.notes: Six pears and three cloves are selected from the source ranges. Sugar and starting water are supplied; wine is a modern 120 ml half-cup. steps: Rinse {{pears}}. Peel them. Halve lengthwise and scoop out all cores and seeds.
Put {{water}} and {{sugar}} in a snug saucepan. Heat gently, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add the pears in one layer, working in batches if needed.

Cover and simmer very gently, turning and basting carefully, until a small knife enters the flesh easily: 1–3 hours for hard winter pears, checking after 45 minutes. Add a little water if the pan dries before the fruit softens.

historical-59de5c1fe7beee5150bbcffd.description: Cooked pear halves receive a caramelized sugar finish just before serving.

ingredients.name: medium firm pears, about 170 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use firm pears of similar size; dessert pears soften sooner than hard winter cooking varieties. Check tenderness rather than relying only on time.

steps: Rinse {{pears}}. Peel them. Halve lengthwise and scoop out all cores and seeds.
Put {{water}} and {{sugar}} in a snug saucepan. Heat gently, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add the pears in one layer, working in batches if needed.
Cover and simmer very gently, turning and basting carefully, until a small knife enters the flesh easily: 15–30 minutes for halves. Add a little water if the pan dries before the fruit softens.
Lift out the pears. Remove any whole spices or zest strips. Simmer the liquid uncovered for 5–10 minutes until lightly syrupy, then spoon it over the fruit.

Drain the cooked pears well, retaining their syrup. Spread {{caramel}} in a clean heavy skillet and heat over medium-low heat until it melts and becomes amber; swirl gently rather than stirring dry sugar.

Take the skillet off the heat. Carefully add the drained pears cut-side down, keeping hands away from hot sugar, then spoon in a little reserved warm syrup to loosen the caramel; it may splutter. Turn gently and serve immediately.

ingredients.name: medium firm baking apples, about 180 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use another firm apple of similar size; sweetness and cooking time differ by variety. Avoid substituting very large apples without allowing longer cooking.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of light brown sugar for a caramel-like flavor, or reduce to taste.

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (356°F). Rinse {{apples}}. Remove the cores and seeds with an apple corer, keeping the apples whole. Make a shallow cut through the skin around the middle of each apple to help limit splitting.
Stand the apples in a snug ovenproof dish lined with baking parchment. Divide {{sugar}} among their cavities and scatter any remainder around them. Cover loosely with foil.

Bake for 30–45 minutes, checking after 25 minutes, until a small knife enters the flesh easily. Larger or firmer apples may take longer. Cover loosely with foil if the tops darken before the centers soften. Remove the foil for the final 10 minutes if the fruit is still pale.
Let stand for 5 minutes, then sprinkle with {{icing}} and serve warm.
historical-cd026bebc91036f4f73540dc.notes: The source title is retained as a historical recipe name, not an asserted Portuguese origin. An explicit four-apple batch replaces the unspecified dishful. Baking parchment and a loose cover replace the old silver-plate/camp-oven option. ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

ingredients.name: all-purpose wheat flour
ingredients.substitution: Use an equal weight of a gluten-free all-purpose blend intended for sauces; texture can differ. Do not replace with an equal weight of cornstarch.

ingredients.name: cold drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Unsalted vegetable stock may replace the same volume in a savory sauce, changing its flavor.

ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit, especially when using salted butter or stock; exchange other salt by weight.

ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of black pepper, which leaves visible specks, or omit.

steps: Whisk {{flour}} with {{water|0.25}} in a small saucepan until smooth.
Gradually whisk in the remaining {{water|0.75}}, then add {{butter}} in small pieces.
Return to medium-low heat, whisking until the sauce gently bubbles. Lower the heat and cook 5 minutes, stirring along the bottom, until smooth and thickened. Avoid a hard boil.
Mix in {{salt}}, {{pepper}}.
Remove from the heat and stir in {{vinegar}}. Warm gently if needed, without boiling.
Serve warm. If too thick after standing, whisk in a small splash of the recipe’s liquid to restore the intended pouring consistency.

historical-ea5ce0f8f4e79149f7d33e75.description: Apple cubes and currants bake in an egg-rich batter scented with cinnamon and lemon.

ingredients.name: medium firm apples, about 180 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use another firm apple of similar size; cooking time and sweetness differ.

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour
ingredients.substitution: Use 80 g a gluten-free all-purpose baking blend; texture may differ.

ingredients.name: drinking water

steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (320°F). Use {{butter}} to grease a deep 23 cm baking dish. Peel and core {{apples}} and cut into 2 cm cubes.

Pour into the prepared dish. Bake for 75–90 minutes until the center is set and reaches at least 71°C (160°F); cover loosely if the surface browns too soon.

historical-dd49b2ca85a83c9d7ecb2ede.title: Compot van Peren (Slow-Cooked Winter Pears)
historical-dd49b2ca85a83c9d7ecb2ede.description: Whole winter pears cook slowly with lemon and warm spices until tender.

ingredients.name: small firm winter cooking pears, about 120 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use firm pears of similar size; dessert pears soften sooner than hard winter cooking varieties. Check tenderness rather than relying only on time.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened pear juice in a fruit dish for a sweeter flavor.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Reduce for a less sweet result; this is not a shelf-stable preserve.

ingredients.name: whole cloves
ingredients.substitution: Omit for a milder dish, or use 0.1 g ground cloves per whole clove and leave in the sauce.

ingredients.name: small cinnamon stick
ingredients.substitution: Use 0.25 tsp ground cinnamon per stick; leave ground spice in the sauce.

ingredients.name: thin strips of lemon zest, yellow part only
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of orange zest; remove strips before serving.

steps: Rinse {{pears}}. Peel them. Scoop out the cores and seeds from the base with a melon baller, keeping the pears whole.
Put {{water}} and {{sugar}} in a snug saucepan with {{cloves}}, {{cinnamon}}, {{zest}}. Heat gently, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add the pears in one layer, working in batches if needed.

Cover and simmer very gently, turning and basting carefully, until a small knife enters the flesh easily: 1–3 hours for hard winter pears, checking after 45 minutes. Add a little water if the pan dries before the fruit softens.
Lift out the pears. Remove any whole spices or zest strips. Simmer the liquid uncovered for 5–10 minutes until lightly syrupy, then spoon it over the fruit.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve warm, or cool promptly and refrigerate.

historical-d046b228d1330ca095782e7f.title: Gebraden Appelen (Raisin and Coconut Baked Apples)
historical-d046b228d1330ca095782e7f.description: Peeled apples are filled with cinnamon sugar and raisins, dotted with butter and finished with a little toasted coconut.

ingredients.name: medium firm baking apples, about 180 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use another firm apple of similar size; sweetness and cooking time differ by variety. Avoid substituting very large apples without allowing longer cooking.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of light brown sugar for a caramel-like flavor, or reduce to taste.

ingredients.name: ground cinnamon
ingredients.substitution: Use half the weight of ground allspice for a different flavor, or omit.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened apple juice for a sweeter pan sauce.

ingredients.name: raisins
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of sultanas or finely chopped dried apricots.

ingredients.name: unsweetened desiccated coconut
ingredients.substitution: Use 10 g finely chopped almonds if suitable, or omit.

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (356°F). Peel {{apples}} and remove the cores and seeds, keeping the apples whole. Arrange upright in a snug ovenproof dish.
Mix {{sugar}}, {{cinnamon}} and {{raisins}} and divide among the apple cavities. Dot the tops with {{butter}} and pour {{water}} into the bottom of the dish.
Bake for 30–45 minutes until a knife enters the flesh easily, spooning the pan liquid over the apples halfway through. Add a small splash of water if the pan dries.
Sprinkle {{coconut}} over the apples during the final 5 minutes, watching that it does not burn. Serve warm.

historical-e02b0f72a81d31d493bba0ea.title: Gewelde Boter (Whipped Butter Sauce)
historical-e02b0f72a81d31d493bba0ea.description: Soft butter is beaten with a little lukewarm water into a light, creamy sauce for immediate serving.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: No replacement is needed; increase cooking water only as needed to cover the food.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit; exchange other salt by weight rather than spoon size.

steps: Let {{butter}} soften until easily beaten, around 20–22°C (68–72°F), without melting it. Beat in a bowl until smooth and light.
Dissolve {{salt}} in {{water}}, warmed only to about 30°C (86°F). Beat the water into the butter one teaspoon at a time, incorporating each addition before adding more.
Stop adding liquid temporarily if the mixture separates; cool the bowl briefly and beat until smooth before continuing. Serve immediately. Do not boil or melt the finished sauce.
historical-e02b0f72a81d31d493bba0ea.notes: This is a whipped butter emulsion, not simply melted butter. The source approximate equal-volume water quantity is reduced to 50 ml per 200 g butter, following a documented Dutch 100 g butter to 25 ml water formula. This change is deliberate and disclosed. historical-7908fdad84292603f94d4bbe.title: Nieuwe aardappelen koken (Boiled New Potatoes)
historical-7908fdad84292603f94d4bbe.description: Scraped new potatoes simmer gently and are drained well, keeping their delicate flavor and intact shape.

ingredients.name: small potatoes, scrubbed, about 3–4 cm across
ingredients.substitution: Use a similarly sized potato with the same texture: waxy for intact pieces; floury for ricing. Large whole potatoes need longer cooking.

ingredients.name: cooking water
ingredients.substitution: Use drinking water; stock changes the flavor and salt level. Rinsing water is separate and is discarded.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit if preferred. Different salts can be exchanged by weight, not necessarily by spoon volume.

steps: Prepare {{potatoes}}. Remove sprouts and damaged or green areas; discard extensively green potatoes. Scrape off loose skin under running water, then rinse.
Bring {{water}} to a boil in a saucepan that holds the potatoes comfortably. Add {{salt}}. Carefully add the potatoes; water should just cover them. If necessary, add enough hot water to cover.
Reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook about 20–25 minutes, until a thin knife enters the center without resistance. Do not use time alone as the test.
Drain carefully and return to the warm pan off the heat. Leave uncovered for 2–3 minutes, gently shaking once, to release steam. Serve hot.
historical-7908fdad84292603f94d4bbe.notes: The hot-water start and source-specific preparation are retained. Choose a pan and water level that keep the pieces submerged. Quantities not stated by the source, equipment guidance, yield and timing are modern estimates. Not kitchen-tested.

historical-edac6ffd74d450db40a5738c.description: A concentrated butter sauce gains a mild vinegar tang and a small amount of nutmeg.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

ingredients.name: all-purpose wheat flour
ingredients.substitution: Use an equal weight of a gluten-free all-purpose blend intended for sauces; texture can differ. Do not replace with an equal weight of cornstarch.

ingredients.name: cold drinking water

Serve warm. If too thick after standing, whisk in a small splash of the recipe’s liquid to restore the intended pouring consistency.

historical-52f41bf29ae0a347f4c4a86a.description: Butter and a small amount of flour form a rich pouring sauce with a little water.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

ingredients.name: all-purpose wheat flour
ingredients.substitution: Use an equal weight of a gluten-free all-purpose blend intended for sauces; texture can differ. Do not replace with an equal weight of cornstarch.

ingredients.name: cold drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Unsalted vegetable stock may replace the same volume in a savory sauce, changing its flavor.

steps: Whisk {{flour}} with {{water|0.25}} in a small saucepan until smooth.
Gradually whisk in the remaining {{water|0.75}}, then add {{butter}} in small pieces.
Return to medium-low heat, whisking until the sauce gently bubbles. Lower the heat and cook 5 minutes, stirring along the bottom, until smooth and thickened. Avoid a hard boil.
Serve warm. If too thick after standing, whisk in a small splash of the recipe’s liquid to restore the intended pouring consistency.

Two source versions converge on this modern saucepan formula: the covered water-bath variant is replaced with controlled direct heat so the flour can simmer. Both source credits are retained. historical-3b3ae96ff5fc57da1ae07d58.title: Sauce Blanche — Stock and Butter
historical-3b3ae96ff5fc57da1ae07d58.description: A thick, stock-based sauce is cooked from butter and flour, then finished with a fresh pat of butter.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

ingredients.name: all-purpose wheat flour
ingredients.substitution: Use an equal weight of a gluten-free all-purpose blend intended for sauces; texture can differ. Do not replace with an equal weight of cornstarch.

ingredients.name: unsalted light chicken stock
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsalted vegetable stock for a meat-free variation.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit, especially when using salted butter or stock; exchange other salt by weight.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Omit for a less sweet finish; do not replace with the same weight of concentrated sweetener.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

steps: Melt {{butter}} in a small heavy saucepan over low heat. Stir in {{flour}} and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes without browning.
Take off the heat and whisk in {{stock}} a little at a time until smooth.
Return to medium-low heat, whisking until the sauce gently bubbles. Lower the heat and cook 5 minutes, stirring along the bottom, until smooth and thickened. Avoid a hard boil.
Mix in {{salt}}, {{sugar}}.
Remove from the heat and stir in {{finish}}. Warm gently if needed, without boiling.
Serve warm. If too thick after standing, whisk in a small splash of the recipe’s liquid to restore the intended pouring consistency.
historical-3b3ae96ff5fc57da1ae07d58.notes: Unsalted chicken stock is selected from the source’s broth-or-milk-and-water options; sauce remains deliberately thick. The final pat is 5 g. historical-c05a3f9107fa9a80b0506311.title: To Boil Potatoes — Peeled Pieces
historical-c05a3f9107fa9a80b0506311.description: Peeled potato pieces simmer from a cold-water start until tender, then drain and dry briefly before serving.

ingredients.name: peeled potatoes, cut into equal 3 cm pieces
ingredients.substitution: Use a similarly sized potato with the same texture: waxy for intact pieces; floury for ricing. Large whole potatoes need longer cooking.

ingredients.name: cooking water
ingredients.substitution: Use drinking water; stock changes the flavor and salt level. Rinsing water is separate and is discarded.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit if preferred. Different salts can be exchanged by weight, not necessarily by spoon volume.

steps: Prepare {{potatoes}}. Remove sprouts and damaged or green areas; discard extensively green potatoes. Rinse clean.
Place the potatoes in a saucepan with {{water}} and {{salt}}. The water should cover them by about 1 cm; add enough cold water if the pan requires it.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently until tender to the center: about 15–20 minutes for 3 cm pieces.
Drain and let steam escape for 2–3 minutes. Serve hot.
historical-c05a3f9107fa9a80b0506311.notes: A tenderness test replaces dependence on the source’s fixed boiling time. No butter or sauce is required for this base recipe. Quantities not stated by the source, equipment guidance, yield and timing are modern estimates. Not kitchen-tested.

historical-3857f5cc1674d352c0a9c599.title: Unsweetened Apple Sauce
historical-3857f5cc1674d352c0a9c599.description: Apples and water cook down to a simple mashed sauce with no added sugar or fat.

ingredients.name: tart apples, weighed after peeling and coring
ingredients.substitution: Use the same prepared weight of another cooking apple; sweetness and the time needed to soften will vary.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened apple juice for a sweeter sauce with a different flavor.

steps: Cut {{apples}} into roughly 2 cm pieces. Put them in a heavy saucepan with {{water}}.

Bring just to a boil, cover and lower the heat. Simmer for 15–25 minutes, stirring frequently, until the apples collapse easily under a spoon. Add a small splash of water only if the pan begins to dry.
Mash the apples with a potato masher, or press through a sieve for a smoother sauce.
Serve warm, or transfer to shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours at 4°C (40°F) or colder. Freeze portions for longer storage. This is not a canning recipe.
historical-3857f5cc1674d352c0a9c599.notes: The two reviewed sources share only apples and water, simmered and mashed. Missing quantities are supplied; no sugar, spice or fat has been added. historical-43dc05f6e574053436366871.title: Baked Apples with Clove and Lemon Syrup
historical-43dc05f6e574053436366871.description: Whole apples bake in a generously sweetened lemon syrup scented with whole cloves.

ingredients.name: medium firm baking apples, about 180 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use another firm apple of similar size; sweetness and cooking time differ by variety. Avoid substituting very large apples without allowing longer cooking.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of light brown sugar for a caramel-like flavor, or reduce to taste.

ingredients.name: whole cloves
ingredients.substitution: Use 0.5 g ground cloves for a different texture; omit the spice-removal step for ground spice.

ingredients.name: thin strips of lemon zest, yellow part only
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of orange zest; avoid bitter white pith.

ingredients.name: lemon juice
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of orange juice for a sweeter citrus flavor.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened apple juice for a sweeter pan sauce.

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (356°F). Rinse {{apples}}. Remove the cores and seeds with an apple corer, keeping the apples whole. Make a shallow cut through the skin around the middle of each apple to help limit splitting.
Arrange the apples in a deep ovenproof dish in one layer. Scatter {{sugar}} around and into them. Add {{cloves}}, {{zest}}, {{lemon}} and {{water}} to the dish. Cover with foil.
Bake for 40–60 minutes until tender through, basting with the syrup after 25 minutes. Uncover for the final 10 minutes. Add a little water if the syrup begins to catch.
Remove and discard all whole cloves and lemon strips. Rest for 5 minutes and serve with the syrup spooned over the fruit.
historical-43dc05f6e574053436366871.notes: The source one pound of sugar is retained as about 454 g. Twelve medium apples are supplied to define the previously unspecified fruit quantity. Water is added to start a syrup without scorching the sugar. Coring and an oven method complete the truncated source. Missing amounts, oven settings, yields and timings are explicit modern estimates, not exact recovered historical measurements. Not kitchen-tested. Scaling changes ingredient quantities, not temperature or cooking time. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours at 4°C (40°F) or colder.

historical-410bed8021a75655d8648621.title: Baked Apples with Raisins and Cloves
historical-410bed8021a75655d8648621.description: Apples filled with raisins, brown sugar and cinnamon bake with cloves, then chill in their syrup for a soft fruit dessert.

ingredients.name: medium firm baking apples, about 180 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use another firm apple of similar size; sweetness and cooking time differ by variety. Avoid substituting very large apples without allowing longer cooking.

ingredients.name: light brown sugar
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of granulated sugar for a lighter flavor.

ingredients.name: ground cinnamon
ingredients.substitution: Use half the weight of ground allspice for a different flavor, or omit.

ingredients.name: raisins
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of sultanas or finely chopped dried apricots.

ingredients.name: whole cloves
ingredients.substitution: Use 0.3 g ground cloves mixed into the filling; no removal is then needed.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened apple juice for a sweeter pan sauce.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of light brown sugar for a caramel-like flavor, or reduce to taste.

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (356°F). Rinse {{apples}}. Remove the cores and seeds with an apple corer, keeping the apples whole. Make a shallow cut through the skin around the middle of each apple to help limit splitting.

Mix {{brown}}, {{cinnamon}} and {{raisins}} and divide among the cavities. Put {{cloves}} in the dish around the apples so they can be removed later. Add {{water}} and sprinkle the tops with {{sugar}}.

Bake for 30–45 minutes, checking after 25 minutes, until a small knife enters the flesh easily. Larger or firmer apples may take longer. Cover loosely with foil if the tops darken before the centers soften. Spoon the pan liquid over the fruit halfway through; some splitting is consistent with this soft preparation.
Remove all whole cloves. Transfer the apples and syrup to a shallow container, cool briefly, then refrigerate within 2 hours. Chill for at least 1 hour before serving.

historical-29a726d546bdd7a711839bfb.description: Pear quarters gently stew with cloves and a modest amount of sugar.

ingredients.substitution: Use firm pears of similar size; dessert pears soften sooner than hard winter cooking varieties. Check tenderness rather than relying only on time.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened pear juice in a fruit dish for a sweeter flavor.

Put {{water}} and {{sugar}} in a snug saucepan with {{cloves}}. Heat gently, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add the pears in one layer, working in batches if needed.

Rest for 5 minutes and serve warm, or cool promptly and refrigerate.

steps: Rinse {{pears}}. Peel them. Halve lengthwise and scoop out all cores and seeds.

Cover and simmer very gently, turning and basting carefully, until a small knife enters the flesh easily: 1–3 hours for hard winter pears, checking after 45 minutes. Add a little water if the pan dries before the fruit softens.
Lift out the pears. Remove any whole spices or zest strips. Simmer the liquid uncovered for 5–10 minutes until lightly syrupy, then spoon it over the fruit.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve warm, or cool promptly and refrigerate.

ingredients.substitution: Use another firm apple of similar size; sweetness and cooking time differ by variety. Avoid substituting very large apples without allowing longer cooking.

ingredients.substitution: Use 80 g pitted dates for a sweeter filling; they may soften faster.

steps: Put {{prunes}} and {{water}} in a small saucepan. Simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until the fruit is soft. Drain, retaining the cooking liquid, and chop the prunes.

Heat the oven to 180°C (356°F). Rinse {{apples}}. Remove the cores and seeds with an apple corer, keeping the apples whole. Make a shallow cut through the skin around the middle of each apple to help limit splitting.
Fill the cavities with the softened prunes. Mix {{sugar}} with {{cinnamon}} and divide over the filling. Pour the reserved prune liquid into the dish.

Bake for 30–45 minutes, checking after 25 minutes, until a small knife enters the flesh easily. Larger or firmer apples may take longer. Cover loosely with foil if the tops darken before the centers soften. Baste once and add a splash of water if the dish dries.

historical-4e59f40a0ce22e484a6251db.description: Light stock sauce is finished with sour cream and chopped dill for a tangy herbal accompaniment.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

ingredients.name: all-purpose wheat flour
ingredients.substitution: Use an equal weight of a gluten-free all-purpose blend intended for sauces; texture can differ. Do not replace with an equal weight of cornstarch.

ingredients.name: unsalted light chicken stock
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsalted vegetable stock for a meat-free variation.

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.substitution: Use 60 g full-fat plain yogurt; keep below a boil to reduce splitting.

Take off the heat and whisk in {{stock}} a little at a time until smooth.
Return to medium-low heat, whisking until the sauce gently bubbles. Lower the heat and cook 5 minutes, stirring along the bottom, until smooth and thickened. Avoid a hard boil.
Remove from the heat and stir in {{sour}}, {{dill}}. Warm gently if needed, without boiling.
Serve warm. If too thick after standing, whisk in a small splash of the recipe’s liquid to restore the intended pouring consistency.

historical-c248ce777dd72a880671f99c.title: Boiled Potatoes in Their Skins
historical-c248ce777dd72a880671f99c.description: Small potatoes cook in their skins until tender, then drain and steam-dry before serving.

ingredients.name: dry long-grain white rice
ingredients.substitution: Use another non-parboiled white long-grain rice and follow its doneness cues. Brown, parboiled and quick-cooking rice need different timings and liquid ratios.

historical-741e9e16fa61611d0e3c972d.description: Slow-simmered lamb’s feet are deboned and served in their gelatin-rich cooking broth, finished with lemon, butter and egg yolk.

ingredients.name: butcher-cleaned lamb’s feet, scalded, dehaired and trimmed
ingredients.substitution: Ask a butcher for cleaned lamb or sheep feet. Mature sheep feet may need longer cooking; boneless lamb is not an equivalent replacement.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: No replacement is needed; increase cooking water only as needed to cover the food.

ingredients.name: strained lamb-foot cooking broth, reserved from this recipe
ingredients.substitution: Use the broth produced in the preceding steps; plain water lacks its gelatin and flavor.

steps: Place {{feet}} in a large pot with {{water}}, adding more water only if needed to cover. Bring to a boil, skim off surface foam, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Cover loosely and simmer for 2–4 hours, or longer if needed, until the skin and connective tissue are very tender and pull easily from the bones. Top up with water to keep submerged.

Lift out the feet and cool only until safe to handle. Remove every bone and piece of hard gristle carefully; cut the edible soft tissue into 2 cm pieces. Strain the cooking liquid through a fine sieve.
Return the deboned meat to a clean pan. Measure {{broth}} from the strained cooking liquid and add it to the meat. Add {{salt}}, {{pepper}} and {{lemon}}, and simmer for 5 minutes.

Whisk {{yolks}} in a bowl. Gradually whisk in several spoonfuls of hot broth, then return to the pan. Stir gently until the sauce reaches 74°C (165°F), without boiling. Remove from the heat and stir in {{butter}}. Serve immediately.

steps: Bring {{water}} to a gentle simmer in a wide saucepan, with enough depth to submerge the eggs.
Toast {{bread}}; spread with {{butter}} and then {{anchovy}}. Keep warm.

Crack {{eggs}} into separate cups. Slide gently into barely simmering water, keeping them apart; cook no more than four at a time. Check from 4 minutes and continue until whites and yolks are firm, usually 5–7 minutes. For pasteurized shell eggs only, 3–4 minutes gives a softer yolk. Lift with a slotted spoon and drain.

historical-3cd9725ee236e6684da4a259.title: Tojás Ülepedve (Eggs with Sour Cream, Anchovies and Pickles)
historical-3cd9725ee236e6684da4a259.description: Eggs bake over sour cream with anchovy strips and tart cucumber pickle, retaining the source’s salty, tangy combination.

ingredients.name: large hen eggs
ingredients.substitution: Use large pasteurized shell eggs for a soft-yolk option. Liquid egg substitute cannot retain this whole-egg shape.

ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of dairy-free butter alternative; check its salt content.

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease a shallow ovenproof dish about 18 cm across with {{butter}} and spread {{cream}} over its base.
Crack {{eggs}} individually into a cup, then slide into the dish without breaking the yolks. Arrange {{anchovy}} between them and {{pickle}} around the edge.
Bake 15–22 minutes, checking from 15 minutes, until whites and yolks are firm. Divide between two plates and serve hot.

historical-5d992a2b07fdbb2743fb8c63.title: Keitettyjä perunoita (Boiled Potato Pieces)
historical-5d992a2b07fdbb2743fb8c63.description: Evenly cut potato pieces simmer in salted water and dry briefly in the warm pan, giving tender centers without added fat.

ingredients.name: peeled potatoes, cut into equal 3 cm pieces
ingredients.substitution: Use a similarly sized potato with the same texture: waxy for intact pieces; floury for ricing. Large whole potatoes need longer cooking.

ingredients.name: cooking water
ingredients.substitution: Use drinking water; stock changes the flavor and salt level. Rinsing water is separate and is discarded.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit if preferred. Different salts can be exchanged by weight, not necessarily by spoon volume.

steps: Prepare {{potatoes}}. Remove sprouts and damaged or green areas; discard extensively green potatoes. Trim to similarly sized rounded pieces; rinse. Perfect spheres are not necessary.
Bring {{water}} to a boil in a saucepan that holds the potatoes comfortably. Add {{salt}}. Carefully add the potatoes; water should just cover them. If necessary, add enough hot water to cover.
Reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook about 15–20 minutes, until a thin knife enters the center without resistance. Do not use time alone as the test.
Drain carefully and return to the warm pan off the heat. Leave uncovered for 2–3 minutes, gently shaking once, to release steam. Serve hot.
historical-5d992a2b07fdbb2743fb8c63.notes: The hot-water start and source-specific preparation are retained. Choose a pan and water level that keep the pieces submerged. Quantities not stated by the source, equipment guidance, yield and timing are modern estimates. Not kitchen-tested.

historical-068bd35af3417a6ecc7d4800.title: Valkea Kastike (Milk and Cream Sauce)
historical-068bd35af3417a6ecc7d4800.description: A light milk sauce is enriched with cream for a smooth, gently seasoned finish.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

ingredients.name: all-purpose wheat flour
ingredients.substitution: Use an equal weight of a gluten-free all-purpose blend intended for sauces; texture can differ. Do not replace with an equal weight of cornstarch.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened soy milk for a dairy-free variation; flavor and thickening may differ.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit, especially when using salted butter or stock; exchange other salt by weight.

ingredients.name: ground white pepper
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of black pepper, which leaves visible specks, or omit.

ingredients.name: heavy cream
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of light cream for a less rich sauce; it may be thinner.

steps: Melt {{butter}} in a small heavy saucepan over low heat. Stir in {{flour}} and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes without browning.
Take off the heat and whisk in {{milk}} a little at a time until smooth.
Return to medium-low heat, whisking until the sauce gently bubbles. Lower the heat and cook 5 minutes, stirring along the bottom, until smooth and thickened. Avoid a hard boil.
Mix in {{salt}}, {{pepper}}.
Remove from the heat and stir in {{cream}}. Warm gently if needed, without boiling.
Serve warm. If too thick after standing, whisk in a small splash of the recipe’s liquid to restore the intended pouring consistency.
historical-068bd35af3417a6ecc7d4800.notes: Equivalent milk/cream formulations are combined. The later source’s egg-and-lemon finish is retained as a variation; it is not presented as classic hollandaise. Missing or ambiguous source amounts, modern ingredient choices, sauce portions and timings are explicit adaptation estimates, not exact recovered historical measurements. Not kitchen-tested. Serve freshly made; scaling changes quantities, not temperature or cooking time.

historical-55b7dbbc2fab113cc67b867d.title: Rice for Soup (Lihalientä riisiryynejä seassa)
historical-55b7dbbc2fab113cc67b867d.description: Plain rice is boiled, drained and briefly rinsed as a component to add to hot soup; this recipe does not make broth.

ingredients.name: dry long-grain white rice
ingredients.substitution: Use another non-parboiled white long-grain rice and follow its doneness cues. Brown, parboiled and quick-cooking rice need different timings and liquid ratios.

ingredients.name: cooking water
ingredients.substitution: Use drinking water; stock changes the flavor and salt level. Rinsing water is separate and is discarded.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit if preferred. Different salts can be exchanged by weight, not necessarily by spoon volume.

steps: Rinse {{rice}} in a sieve under cold drinking water until the runoff is mostly clear.
Bring {{water}} and {{salt}} to a boil in a saucepan. Add the drained rice and return to a gentle boil.
Cook uncovered until the grains are tender but separate, checking from 10 minutes for basmati or 12 minutes for other long-grain white rice; allow up to 20 minutes if needed.
Drain in a fine sieve. Rinse briefly with clean cool water to stop cooking, as in the source, then drain well. Add directly to hot soup and heat through before serving; soup is a separate recipe.

historical-6b93e1af8b5be685d56e023e.title: Enkelt Äppelmos (Sweet Lemon Apple Sauce)
historical-6b93e1af8b5be685d56e023e.description: A sweet, thick apple sauce retains the source ratio of one part sugar to two parts prepared apple, with lemon juice and zest.

ingredients.substitution: Use the same prepared weight of another cooking apple; sweetness and the time needed to soften will vary.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened apple juice for a sweeter sauce with a different flavor.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Reduce to taste for a less sweet sauce; this is a refrigerated food, not a shelf-stable preserve.

ingredients.name: lemon juice
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of lime juice for a different citrus flavor.

ingredients.name: finely grated lemon zest, yellow part only
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of orange zest, or omit.

steps: Cut {{apples}} into small pieces and put in a heavy saucepan with {{water}}, {{sugar}}, {{lemon}} and {{zest}}.

Warm gently, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Simmer over low heat for 25–35 minutes, stirring frequently along the bottom, until the apples break down to a thick pulp. Add a little water only if needed to prevent scorching.
Mash thoroughly or pass through a sieve. If too thin, simmer uncovered for a few more minutes while stirring.
Serve warm, or transfer to shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours at 4°C (40°F) or colder. Freeze portions for longer storage. This is not a canning recipe.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar

ingredients.name: drinking water

Cool promptly in shallow containers and refrigerate, or freeze portions.
