historical-b42799f5292cd308f900f0dd.title: Förlorade Ägg (Shallow-Poached Eggs on Fried Bread)
historical-b42799f5292cd308f900f0dd.description: Shallow-poached eggs are drained and served on bread fried in butter; a dry-toast variation is retained.

ingredients.name: large hen eggs
ingredients.substitution: Use large pasteurized shell eggs for a soft-yolk option. Liquid egg substitute cannot retain this whole-egg shape.

ingredients.name: poaching water
ingredients.substitution: Use drinking water; adjust depth to fit the pan. This water is drained, not consumed.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit; exchange other salt by weight rather than spoon volume.

ingredients.name: white wine vinegar
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of distilled white vinegar, or omit for a milder flavor.

ingredients.name: bread slices, about 35 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use similarly sized gluten-free bread; toasting time may differ.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of dairy-free butter alternative; check its salt content.

steps: Bring {{water}}, {{salt}} and {{vinegar}} to a boil, then lower to a barely moving simmer. Use a wide pan with about 2 cm water depth.

Check from 4 minutes and continue until whites and yolks are firm, usually 5–7 minutes. For pasteurized shell eggs only, 3–4 minutes gives a softer yolk. Lift with a slotted spoon and drain.
Melt {{butter}} in a separate frying pan over medium heat. Fry {{bread}} for 1–2 minutes per side until golden, in batches if needed.
Put a drained egg on each bread slice and serve hot.

Cold rinsing and decorative trimming are omitted for immediate hot service. Supplied quantities, yield and times are modern estimates, not recovered source facts. historical-d4ae7bdbdf2061ac22e1c6f3.title: Helkokta Äpplen (Whole Stewed Apples)
historical-d4ae7bdbdf2061ac22e1c6f3.description: Whole apples cook gently in a clear sugar syrup and are served chilled with whipped cream.

ingredients.name: medium firm apples, about 180 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use another firm apple of similar size; cooking time and sweetness differ.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Reduce to taste; this is not a shelf-stable preserve.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened apple juice for a sweeter fruit dish.

ingredients.name: heavy cream
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of plant-based cream suitable for the stated use.

steps: Rinse {{apples}}, peel and remove every core and seed. Keep the apples whole.
In a snug pan, heat {{water}} with {{sugar}}, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add the apples in one layer, working in batches if needed.

Cover and simmer gently, turning carefully halfway through, until a knife enters easily but the fruit holds its shape: about 20–35 minutes. Baste frequently; add a little water if the liquid becomes too thick before the fruit softens.
Lift the apples onto a serving dish. Simmer the liquid uncovered for 3–8 minutes until lightly syrupy, then spoon it over the fruit.
Cool briefly, then refrigerate within 2 hours. Chill for at least 1 hour before serving.
Whip {{cream}} until soft peaks form and serve alongside the chilled apples.

ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

ingredients.name: all-purpose wheat flour
ingredients.substitution: Use an equal weight of a gluten-free all-purpose blend intended for sauces; texture can differ. Do not replace with an equal weight of cornstarch.

steps: Melt {{butter}} in a small heavy saucepan over low heat. Stir in {{flour}} and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes without browning.

historical-355ce4078f46f35dbfc915a9.description: Cored apples bake in a buttered dish with a light sprinkle of sugar, keeping the fruit flavor prominent.

ingredients.name: medium firm baking apples, about 180 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use another firm apple of similar size; sweetness and cooking time differ by variety. Avoid substituting very large apples without allowing longer cooking.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative.

ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of light brown sugar for a caramel-like flavor, or reduce to taste.

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (356°F). Rinse {{apples}}. Remove the cores and seeds with an apple corer, keeping the apples whole. Make a shallow cut through the skin around the middle of each apple to help limit splitting.
Use {{butter}} to coat the inside of a snug ovenproof dish. Stand the apples in it and sprinkle evenly with {{sugar}}. Cover loosely with foil.

Bake for 30–45 minutes, checking after 25 minutes, until a small knife enters the flesh easily. Larger or firmer apples may take longer. Cover loosely with foil if the tops darken before the centers soften. Uncover for the last 10 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve warm, or cool briefly and refrigerate for serving cold.

historical-47594cfda891841509685ecc.description: Peeled apples are coated in crisp rusk crumbs, filled with sugar and served chilled with vanilla-scented whipped cream.

ingredients.name: medium firm baking apples, about 180 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use another firm apple of similar size; sweetness and cooking time differ by variety. Avoid substituting very large apples without allowing longer cooking.

ingredients.substitution: Use 60 g fine dry breadcrumbs, or gluten-free crumbs if needed; sweetness and texture differ.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of light brown sugar for a caramel-like flavor, or reduce to taste.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative.

ingredients.name: cold heavy whipping cream
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of a plant-based cream specifically suitable for whipping; texture and flavor differ.

ingredients.name: vanilla sugar
ingredients.substitution: Use 8 g granulated sugar plus 1 ml vanilla extract.

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (356°F). Peel {{apples}} and carefully scoop out the cores and seeds, leaving a base in each apple to hold the filling.
Coat the damp peeled apples with {{rusks}}, pressing gently. Use {{butter|0.5}} to grease a snug ovenproof dish and stand the apples in it.

Bake for 35–50 minutes until tender, uncovering for the final 10 minutes to crisp the crumbs. Cover again if the crumbs darken too quickly.
Cool briefly, transfer to a shallow covered container and refrigerate within 2 hours. Chill for at least 1 hour.
Whip {{cream}} with {{vanilla}} until soft peaks form. Serve with the chilled apples.

historical-0d8cc30aa57193ec432070f0.description: Pan-fried bacon is topped with drained poached eggs for a simple savory breakfast.

steps: Rinse {{rice}} in a sieve under cold drinking water until the runoff is mostly clear.
Bring {{water}} and {{salt}} to a boil in a saucepan. Add the drained rice and return to a gentle boil.
Cook uncovered until the grains are tender but separate, checking from 10 minutes for basmati or 12 minutes for other long-grain white rice; allow up to 20 minutes if needed.
Drain in a fine sieve. Return to the warm pan off the heat for 3 minutes so excess moisture can evaporate. Gently loosen and serve separately from the main dish.
historical-241f3d238a6aa69aa8f6d61e.notes: Rice type, batch size, water and salt quantities are supplied as modern choices. The source’s excess-water method is retained; rice-package timing and actual tenderness take priority over a historical fixed time. Quantities not stated by the source, equipment guidance, yield and timing are modern estimates. Not kitchen-tested.

historical-24904b50d69ba65309eccc39.title: Old-Fashioned Oven Apple Sauce
historical-24904b50d69ba65309eccc39.description: Chopped apples slowly reduce in the oven with white sugar and water, developing a deeper fruit flavor.

ingredients.name: medium firm apples, about 180 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use another firm apple of similar size; cooking time and sweetness differ.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of the other sugar for a different flavor, or reduce to taste.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened apple juice for a sweeter fruit dish.

steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (320°F). Peel and core {{apples}}, then cut into 2 cm pieces.
Put the fruit in a covered ovenproof casserole with {{sugar}} and {{water}}. Stir, cover and bake for 90 minutes.
Stir carefully and continue for 30–60 minutes, uncovering for the last 20 minutes if too wet, until very soft and reduced. Add a splash of water if the edges catch.
Mash to the desired texture and serve warm, or cool promptly in shallow containers and refrigerate.
historical-24904b50d69ba65309eccc39.notes: The source dozen is halved. Its imprecise heaping coffeecup sugar and cup water become explicit modern amounts. Time varies with fruit moisture. Missing quantities, yields and timings are disclosed modern estimates, not recovered historical measures. Not kitchen-tested. Scaling changes quantities, not time or temperature. Refrigerate in shallow containers within 2 hours at 4°C (40°F) or colder; freeze for longer storage. Not a canning recipe.
historical-24904b50d69ba65309eccc39.source: The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887), F.L. Gillette. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/13923 SavorShelf measured adaptation.

historical-a0d201246851b504a8dc21e4.title: Sautéed Pears with Chilled Chocolate-Caramel Sauce
historical-a0d201246851b504a8dc21e4.description: Browned pear quarters are paired with a chilled chocolate sauce enriched with cream and a butter-caramel finish.

ingredients.name: medium firm pears, about 170 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use firm pears of similar size; dessert pears soften sooner than hard winter cooking varieties. Check tenderness rather than relying only on time.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative.

ingredients.name: sweet eating chocolate, chopped
ingredients.substitution: Use 57 g semisweet chocolate for a darker, less sweet sauce.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Reduce for a less sweet result; this is not a shelf-stable preserve.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened soy milk; flavor and texture differ.

ingredients.name: arrowroot starch
ingredients.substitution: Use 3 g cornstarch; simmer for 1 minute to cook it.

ingredients.name: heavy cream
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of a plant-based cream suited to the stated use.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Omit if using salted butter.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Reduce for a less sweet result; this is not a shelf-stable preserve.

ingredients.name: vanilla extract
ingredients.substitution: Use 1 g vanilla paste, or omit.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened pear juice in a fruit dish for a sweeter flavor.

steps: Combine {{chocolate}}, {{sugar}} and {{milk}} in a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water, keeping the bowl above the water. Stir until melted and smooth, about 5 minutes.
Mix {{arrowroot}} with {{cream}} and whisk into the warm chocolate mixture with {{salt}}. Continue heating and stirring for 5–10 minutes until lightly thickened.

In a small light-colored saucepan, heat {{caramelsugar}} with {{caramelwater}} until the sugar dissolves. Stop stirring and cook until golden amber. Remove from the heat and carefully whisk in {{caramelbutter}}; the mixture will bubble.
Carefully whisk the warm chocolate mixture into the caramel a little at a time; it may bubble. Stir in {{vanilla}}, pour into a shallow container, cool briefly and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Just before serving, peel {{pears}}, quarter and remove cores. Melt {{butter}} in a skillet and sauté the quarters for 8–12 minutes, turning, until golden and tender. Serve with the chilled sauce.
historical-a0d201246851b504a8dc21e4.notes: Separate cooking and caramel butter quantities are supplied. Modern 300 ml milk and 60 ml cream replace source cups. Granulated sugar replaces powdered sugar in the caramel for more predictable browning; the chocolate, arrowroot and chilled-sauce character remain. Missing amounts, oven settings, yields and timings are explicit modern adaptation estimates, not exact historical conversions. Not kitchen-tested. Scaling changes quantities, not cooking time or temperature. Refrigerate in shallow containers within 2 hours at 4°C (40°F) or colder; this is not a canning recipe. The caramel sugar is cooked with a little water before the butter is added, replacing the less controlled source simultaneous butter-and-sugar browning.
historical-a0d201246851b504a8dc21e4.source: The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896), Fannie Merritt Farmer. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/65061 SavorShelf measured adaptation.

historical-8788d6cca0f07cd02dbcbd7f.title: Clove-Spiced Apple Sauce
historical-8788d6cca0f07cd02dbcbd7f.description: Tart apples simmer with sugar and whole cloves, then are mashed into a strongly aromatic sauce.

ingredients.name: tart apples, weighed after peeling and coring
ingredients.substitution: Use the same prepared weight of another cooking apple; sweetness and the time needed to soften will vary.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened apple juice for a sweeter sauce with a different flavor.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Reduce to taste for a less sweet sauce; this is a refrigerated food, not a shelf-stable preserve.

ingredients.name: whole cloves
ingredients.substitution: Use 0.75 g ground cloves for a slightly different texture; do not strain out ground spice.

steps: Cut {{apples}} into 2 cm pieces. Put them in a heavy saucepan with {{water}} and {{sugar}}.
Tie {{cloves}} in a small piece of food-safe cheesecloth and add to the pan, or count them carefully so all can be removed. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover loosely and cook for 20–30 minutes, stirring frequently, until the apples are very soft. Add a small splash of water if the bottom begins to dry.
Remove and discard the clove bundle or all whole cloves, then mash the fruit to the desired texture.
Serve warm, or transfer to shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours at 4°C (40°F) or colder. Freeze portions for longer storage. This is not a canning recipe.
historical-8788d6cca0f07cd02dbcbd7f.notes: Eight source apples become 1200 g prepared fruit; one cup of sugar is assigned 200 g. The original eight cloves remain, with an explicit removal step to avoid leaving whole spices in the finished sauce. Missing amounts, portion yields and timings are disclosed modern estimates, not exact recovered historical measurements. Not kitchen-tested. Scaling changes quantities, not cooking time or temperature.

historical-a99d5a7f8bf20cf1d7d7b95b.title: Stewed Apple Halves in Reduced Syrup
historical-a99d5a7f8bf20cf1d7d7b95b.description: Firm apple halves are gently poached, then chilled beneath a reduced lemon syrup.

ingredients.name: medium firm apples, about 180 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use another firm apple of similar size; cooking time and sweetness differ.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Reduce to taste; this is not a shelf-stable preserve.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened apple juice for a sweeter fruit dish.

ingredients.name: lemon juice
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of lime juice for a different citrus flavor.

steps: Rinse {{apples}}, peel and remove every core and seed. Cut into halves.
In a snug pan, heat {{water}} with {{sugar}}, {{lemon}}, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add the apples in one layer, working in batches if needed.

Cover and simmer gently, turning carefully halfway through, until a knife enters easily but the fruit holds its shape: about 10–20 minutes. Baste frequently; add a little water if the liquid becomes too thick before the fruit softens.
Lift the apples onto a serving dish. Simmer the liquid uncovered for 3–8 minutes until lightly syrupy, then spoon it over the fruit.
Cool briefly, then refrigerate within 2 hours. Chill for at least 1 hour before serving.
historical-a99d5a7f8bf20cf1d7d7b95b.notes: The source cup sugar per six apples becomes 200 g; water and lemon amounts are supplied. A syrup-texture endpoint replaces the rigid extra half-hour boil, which could over-concentrate a small modern batch. Missing quantities, yields and timings are disclosed modern estimates, not recovered historical measures. Not kitchen-tested. Scaling changes quantities, not time or temperature. Refrigerate in shallow containers within 2 hours at 4°C (40°F) or colder; freeze for longer storage. Not a canning recipe.

historical-83fddb7be47353fc161e3533.title: Stewed Pears with Cinnamon, Lemon and Cream
historical-83fddb7be47353fc161e3533.description: Pear halves simmer with cloves, cinnamon and lemon, then are served with cream and reduced syrup.

ingredients.name: medium firm pears, about 170 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use firm pears of similar size; dessert pears soften sooner than hard winter cooking varieties. Check tenderness rather than relying only on time.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened pear juice in a fruit dish for a sweeter flavor.

ingredients.substitution: Reduce for a less sweet result; this is not a shelf-stable preserve.

ingredients.substitution: Omit for a milder dish, or use 0.1 g ground cloves per whole clove and leave in the sauce.

ingredients.name: small cinnamon stick
ingredients.substitution: Use 0.25 tsp ground cinnamon per stick; leave ground spice in the sauce.

ingredients.name: lemon juice
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of lime juice for a different flavor.

ingredients.name: heavy cream
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of a plant-based cream suited to the stated use.

steps: Rinse {{pears}}. Peel them. Halve lengthwise and scoop out all cores and seeds.
Put {{water}} and {{sugar}} in a snug saucepan with {{cloves}}, {{cinnamon}}, {{lemon}}. Heat gently, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add the pears in one layer, working in batches if needed.
Cover and simmer very gently, turning and basting carefully, until a small knife enters the flesh easily: 15–30 minutes for halves. Add a little water if the pan dries before the fruit softens.
Lift out the pears. Remove any whole spices or zest strips. Simmer the liquid uncovered for 5–10 minutes until lightly syrupy, then spoon it over the fruit.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve warm, or cool promptly and refrigerate.
Serve with {{cream}} poured alongside.

historical-5778d1032c4352a93d8a40af.title: Thin White Sauce — Boston Formula
historical-5778d1032c4352a93d8a40af.description: A light butter-and-milk sauce has just enough flour to coat gently.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

ingredients.name: all-purpose wheat flour
ingredients.substitution: Use an equal weight of a gluten-free all-purpose blend intended for sauces; texture can differ. Do not replace with an equal weight of cornstarch.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened soy milk for a dairy-free variation; flavor and thickening may differ.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit, especially when using salted butter or stock; exchange other salt by weight.

ingredients.name: ground white pepper
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of black pepper, which leaves visible specks, or omit.

steps: Melt {{butter}} in a small heavy saucepan over low heat. Stir in {{flour}} and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes without browning.
Take off the heat and whisk in {{milk}} a little at a time until smooth.
Return to medium-low heat, whisking until the sauce gently bubbles. Lower the heat and cook 5 minutes, stirring along the bottom, until smooth and thickened. Avoid a hard boil.
Mix in {{salt}}, {{pepper}}.
Serve warm. If too thick after standing, whisk in a small splash of the recipe’s liquid to restore the intended pouring consistency.

historical-afcfb35f8bc1bdc0a661fb55.title: To Boil Rice — Modern Absorption Adaptation
historical-afcfb35f8bc1bdc0a661fb55.description: White long-grain rice cooks in measured salted water and rests covered; this is a modern adaptation of the source’s boil-and-dry method.

ingredients.name: dry white basmati rice
ingredients.substitution: Use another non-parboiled white long-grain rice and follow its doneness cues. Brown, parboiled and quick-cooking rice need different timings and liquid ratios.

ingredients.name: cooking water
ingredients.substitution: Use drinking water; stock changes the flavor and salt level. Rinsing water is separate and is discarded.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit if preferred. Different salts can be exchanged by weight, not necessarily by spoon volume.

steps: Rinse {{rice}} in a sieve under cold drinking water until the runoff is mostly clear.
Combine the drained rice with {{water}} and {{salt}} in a small, heavy saucepan with a close-fitting lid. Bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce to the lowest heat and cook about 12–15 minutes until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender. If still firm and dry, add 15–30 ml hot water and cook a few minutes longer.
Remove from the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes, then separate the grains gently with a fork. Do not multiply cooking time when scaling; use a suitable pan.
historical-afcfb35f8bc1bdc0a661fb55.notes: The source’s draining/coals stage is replaced with a measured absorption method and covered rest. The old cup ratio is not claimed as an exact modern conversion. Quantities not stated by the source, equipment guidance, yield and timing are modern estimates. Not kitchen-tested.
